parameter.name: anyField
parameter.description: One text matched against any of these, so a party matching one of them is found (the other parameters still narrow the find): an organization's name; a person's first or last name, or first and last name together in either order ('Kim Lund', 'Lund, Kim'); a current email address; a current phone number by its digits, whatever the formatting and with or without a leading country code ('+1 (801) 555-0123', '801.555.0123' and '5550123' all find 801 555-0123; at least three digits, matching the number's trailing part); and the people whose current contact or employee relationship (PrtContact, PrtEmployee) is to an organization of that name the user may see. leadingWildcard applies to the names and the email. One find of distinct parties, so the count is exact (the people of organizations and the phone matches are found first, up to 5000 each).

parameter.name: hasRole
parameter.description: True finds only parties with a PartyRole of any type (the directory's customers, suppliers, contacts and the like). The user's personal contacts, which have no role, are not left out by it: personalContacts=exclude does that.

parameter.name: personalContacts
parameter.description: Personal contacts (Party.privateOwnerUserId) are only ever the current user's: empty includes the user's own with the directory, 'exclude' leaves them out, 'only' finds only them.

parameter.name: leadingWildcard
parameter.description: Defaults for false for DB query performance reasons.

service.description: The header badge counts of a user, for the theme value STRT_SHELL_COUNTS_SERVICE (the framework's org.moqui.impl.ShellServices.get#ShellCounts and publish#ShellCounts call it with userId and send counts as it is). Written over each user's own state, not on get#UserNoticeCounts, which counts declined events and completed tasks and reads messages by toPartyId only. counts: - today: the overdue and due today items of the user's Today (mantle.work.WorkEffortServices.get#UserTodayItems: tasks, activities and events; the apps' today-sources are not counted), the Today badge - overdue: the overdue ones of those - notifications: the user's unviewed notifications of the Notifications inbox (topics whose inboxEnumId is not NinUpdates, and every topic with an approve service), the Notifications badge - approvals: the unviewed ones whose topic has an approve service, a part of notifications - updates: the unviewed notifications of the automatic Updates inbox (NinUpdates topics: record-update feeds, system messages, job reports), no badge (count#UserNotifications) - messages: the unread internal messages and Inbox-delivered mailbox posts (mantle.party.CommunicationServices.count#UnreadInternalMessages), the Messages badge - email: the unread mail in the Inbox folders of the user's mail accounts, not snoozed or archived (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.count#UnreadEmail), the Mail badge - chat: the unread chat messages and mentions that count for the user (org.moqui.impl.ChatServices.get#UnreadCounts total: the unread of rooms at notification level all, the mentions of rooms at mentions or muted, nothing at none), the Chat badge. The framework's ChatServices publish the counts of the users whose chat counts change (publish#ChatCounts), so no entity ECA is needed for it. Each part stands alone: one that fails is logged by name, null in counts and named in failedParts. The counts read only the user's own rows, with authorization disabled; another user's counts only for internal work, with authorization already disabled.

A user's unviewed notifications (the current user's by default), by inbox (NotificationTopic.inboxEnumId): updateCount, those of the automatic Updates inbox (NinUpdates topics without an approve service); notificationCount, the rest (the Notifications inbox, the default, and every topic with an approve service); approvalCount, those whose topic has an approve service, so wait on the user's decision, a part of notificationCount. The approve and refuse services get recordEntityName, recordId, the message's messageJson map and, for a refuse, reason (IronStone R23). The rows are read with authorization disabled, for that user only; another user's counts only with authorization disabled already.
